summary.headline: LMW Q4 FY26 revenue rose to ₹854 crore (vs ₹789 crore a year ago) and TMD order book reached ₹3,300 crore, with ~₹2,300 crore active.
summary.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue rose to ₹3,353 crore from ₹3,137 crore and consolidated profit to ₹195 crore from ₹151 crore, with standalone PBT up 42% to ₹221 crore. Q4 standalone revenue was ₹854 crore, up from ₹767 crore in Q3 and ₹789 crore a year ago. Management said textile machinery (TMD) order intake rose sharply in Q4 as cotton spinners' profitability improved, while the machine tool division grew strongly and ATC revenue reached ₹207 crore. Management flagged rising raw material, logistics and commodity costs across the industry, with no price hikes taken in MTD yet.

segments.name: TMD (textile machinery)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹1,801 crore (down ~2%) and profit ₹9.75 crore; Q4 revenue ₹485 crore. Order book ₹3,300 crore (about ₹2,300 crore active), all booked in Q4. FY26 sales mix domestic:exports:spares 66:8:26.

segments.name: Machine tool division (MTD)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 25-28% in FY26 to ~₹1,205 crore for machine tools plus foundry (~10% foundry). Management cited ~11.5% margin in Q4 and no price hikes. Customer mix ~50-52% automotive, ~48% non-automotive; capacity headroom of ~20% and utilisation of 70-75%.

segments.name: ATC (aerospace and precision components)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹207 crore (vs ₹169 crore); Q4 revenue ~₹56 crore with segment result ~₹11 crore (close to 20% margin). Order book ~₹360 crore to be executed over 18 months. About 90% of sales are exports; mix is ~78% metallics and ~22% composites.

segments.name: LMW Global and LMW China
segments.commentary: LMW Global FY26 turnover ₹184 crore with ₹32 crore loss and ₹44 crore order book. LMW China FY26 turnover ₹130 crore, breakeven, and ₹120 crore order book.

guidance_outlook: Management expects a much larger offtake of textile machines as cotton spinners' margins improve, but said it is too early to call a hockey-stick recovery like FY22.
ATC capacity additions are expected to start yielding higher turnover in the second half of FY27.
Management expects MTD margins to continue as turnover grows, and said it will invest for growth once utilisation nears 90%.
Management plans a new, larger ATC facility outside the city centre; ATC capex of about ₹150 crore over five years was referenced for infrastructure only, excluding machinery.
Management aims to rebuild exports to about 23-25% of sales over the next three years, from ~8% in FY26 (per the sales mix).
capex_capacity: Textile machinery capacity utilisation is about 50-55%; machine tool utilisation is about 70-75%, with ~20% headroom in MTD even after Q4 shipments.
Capex of over ₹300 crore was spent in the last three years, mainly for machine tool capacity and modernisation; about 50% of FY26 capex went to ATC.
ATC composites utilisation is about 50%, with headroom to grow.
ATC capex is project-specific and tied to order wins; the new facility is planned to be larger than the current one.
The company is considering an investment of up to US$30 million via a UAE holding company, partly for working capital and partly for export growth (GCC presence for two years).
demand_pricing: Management said the textile industry has improved over the last two months, with good cotton yarn spreads, while crude-based synthetics face challenges. Demand is recovering from Bangladesh, China-linked yarn demand and Turkey.
TMD order book of ₹3,300 crore, all booked in Q4, versus the previous quarter's figure.
No price hikes taken in MTD; margin uplift attributed to operating leverage, with some forex income.
Raw material, logistics, steel, plastics and commodity costs are rising industry-wide; management did not disclose the size of planned price increases.
Import content in machine tools is about 50% of materials, mostly sourced locally in INR, with some USD-linked sourcing.
ATC is about 90% export-driven; customers are Tier-1 aerospace suppliers, and it also supplies ISRO, HAL and defence.

qa_highlights.question: What is the textile outlook and order pipeline, and the MTD growth and ATC order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Textile order book is ₹3,300 crore, all booked in Q4. MTD is continuing to grow with automotive at ~50-52%. ATC booked ₹195 crore; its order book of ~₹360 crore is to be executed over 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is ATC's business, customer qualification cycle, and profit potential?
qa_highlights.answer: ATC has metallics and composites divisions covering engine parts, sheet metal, structures, assemblies and special processes. It is about 90% export-focused. Management said the ~19 certifications required include NADCAP, ISO and customer-specific ones. It does not disclose growth numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Why invest up to US$30 million in a UAE holding company, and what is the payback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the funds are for working capital, which is under pressure because of geopolitics, and for export growth in GCC markets. It cited turning-centre exports of ~₹20 crore and a target of 23-25% exports over three years. No payback period was given.

qa_highlights.question: How can ROCE improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said textile machinery is cyclical with an ~8-year cycle and the business is at a low point. It said ATC has much better ROCE, MTD will improve, and capex is heavy in textile. Management said it will keep investing through downturns.

qa_highlights.question: Is the order book 3,300 crore total with 2,300 crore active? What price hikes are needed to offset raw material costs, and what is the imported content?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed: ₹3,300 crore total, ~₹2,300 crore active. Management would not share the size of price increases. Machine tool import content is about 50%, partly sourced locally in INR.

qa_highlights.question: Could ATC scale to ₹1,000 crore in five years, given a ~₹150 crore capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ₹150 crore figure covers infrastructure only, excluding machinery, and that the new facility could scale beyond ₹300 crore of revenue. It did not give a ₹1,000 crore target.

risks_watch: Volatile crude and geopolitics are hurting synthetic fibre producers and pressuring working capital; banks may limit funding.
Raw material and logistics costs are rising, and availability is a concern (e.g., LPG and some industrial gases); pricing pass-through is unclear.
ATC order book depends on long-term contracts subject to push-outs or pull-ins, and the business is working-capital intensive because raw materials are imported.
Textile recovery may be cyclical and not a sharp rebound; management has not committed to a timeline.
Export contribution fell to ~8% of sales in FY26, against a historical 23-25% target.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the order book, MTD margins and ATC growth, but cautious on textile recovery timing and evasive on pricing, customer names, ATC targets and payback. It described the textile cycle as still at a low point.
key_quotes: We have actually got a significant increase in order book compared to the last quarter.
Whether this again would be, you know, a hockey stick recovery kind of what we have seen in 21-22 that is too early to be mentioned.
So, what you're seeing is pure operational the margin which is coming through because of consistently doing upwards of 100 crores or 300 crores per quarter.
But customer names and the projects would be difficult.

growth.why: Management expects much larger textile machine offtake and ATC capacity to yield higher turnover in H2 FY27, backed by a ₹3,300 crore TMD order book (~₹2,300 crore active) and ATC additions, but no FY27 revenue growth figure was given and the hockey-stick recovery was called too early.
